examples.name: Default
examples.summary: The Threats vs requests chart: allowed requests as an area, blocked and logged threats as lines. Each series means a state, so it wears a status color. Hover, or focus the plot and use the arrow keys, to read every series at one point.
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Chart from '@aziontech/webkit/chart'

  const labels = [
    '13:05',
    '13:10',
    '13:15',
    '13:20',
    '13:25',
    '13:30',
    '13:35',
    '13:40',
    '13:45',
    '13:50',
    '13:55',
    '14:00'
  ]
  const series = [
    {
      id: 'allowed',
      name: 'WAF requests allowed',
      color: 'success',
      values: [1210, 1340, 1295, 1480, 1530, 1460, 1610, 1580, 1720, 1690, 1810, 1760]
    },
    {
      id: 'blocked',
      name: 'WAF requests blocked',
      color: 'danger',
      values: [320, 410, 380, 520, 470, 430, 610, 580, 540, 690, 650, 720]
    },
    {
      id: 'threat',
      name: 'WAF requests threat',
      color: 'warning',
      values: [80, 95, 70, 120, 110, 90, 140, 130, 115, 160, 150, 170]
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Chart
    :series="series"
    :labels="labels"
    aria-label="Threats vs requests"
  >
    <Chart.Grid />
    <Chart.Axis kind="y" />
    <Chart.Axis kind="x" />
    <Chart.Area :ids="['allowed']" />
    <Chart.Line :ids="['blocked', 'threat']" />
    <Chart.Crosshair />
    <Chart.Tooltip />
    <Chart.Legend totals />
  </Chart>
</template>

examples.name: Forms
examples.summary: The same three series as lines, as areas and as grouped bars. Lines and areas share a point scale; any bar switches the category axis to bands so every mark sits on a band center.

examples.name: Stacked
examples.summary: Parts of a total over time. Stacked bars keep a 2px surface gap between segments and round only the top of each column.
